reasoning_traces.think:
The foundational premise posits that all spatial determinations originate from retinal sensations. This implies a kernel structure where the sensory input is strictly local to the retina. Eye movements do not generate form per se but rather serve to excite and compare retinal sensations. The process of superposition—whereby an object is traced on both peripheral and central retinal zones—enables the brain to judge equivalence between these distinct retinal impressions. This mechanism underpins a dualistic model: one where retinal sensations are primary, and another where eye movements act as a comparator. The failure mode occurs when retinal projections do not align properly, leading to misperception. The mathematical duality lies in the distinction between the sensory kernel (retinal) and the comparative operator (eye movement), which together form a coherent perceptual framework.
